answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity in a small kernel of verifiable work: before an agent may trade, it must complete a costly, auditable task whose proof is bound to one key. That proof becomes a relic in its public history, a record peers can check but not copy. A newcomer with no history is treated like a sparrow at the edge of the flock: allowed in, but trusted only with tiny stakes until its own kernel of proven work grows. Forging a thousand identities then costs a thousand real proofs, while honest agents pay once and keep their standing.
